chapter.title_hebrew: הענף הג': דעת גדולי עולם על כתיבת תושבע"פ
chapter.title_english: Branch Three: Views of Great Sages on the Writing of Oral Law

paragraphs.hebrew_raw: חדרים, על כל פרק ופרק כשיגיע לידו לדבר מרבינו שרירא, ימלא פיו תהלתו, הן בתולדות הערוך, הן בתולדות בנו ר"ה גאון, הן בהקדמתו המלאה לה רוח דעת ויראת ה' שבתשו' הגאונים דפוס ברלין עד שכתב על אגרת ר"ש שביוחסין שאנו בה וז"ל: "והיא נפלאה מאד בביאור שנות קדמונינו חז"ל ובבירור כל דבר על אמתתו והבאת מאמרי התלמוד הנאותים לדבריו, וכל חוקר בקדמוניות ישמח וישבע מעדנים בקראו בה" (תולדות ר"ן בה"ע הערה ל"ב) אלו דברי חוקר זמנינו יהי ה' אלהיו עמו ויעל. ד. והיה אם לא נאמין לקול האות הראשון הוא ר"ש גאון ז"ל בב' תשו' הנז"ל, כי אפשר יבואו עלינו בטענות הזיוף לזאת שלפנינו, ולאגרתו שביוחסין עם נוסח החשוך שבחופש מטמונים, כי כסו פניו חרולים חרולים וכנז"ל, נאמין לקול האות האחרון רבי' שמואל הנגיד ז"ל תלמידם של גאונים שבאמצעות ר"ן מקירוואן קנה לו שם טוב זה ע"י שאלותיו לר"ה גאון ז"ל וקבלת תשובותיו ממנו, והוא אילן גדול לסמוך עליו בענין זה יותר מרש"י וסיעתיה באלף ידות, וצא ולמד מה כתב גאון דורנו הנז"ל בתולדות ר"הג ז"ל הערה ב' וז"ל: "אעפ"י שאגרת ר"ש שביוחסין היתה למקור תמיד לס' הקבלה להראב"ד כמו שהראתי בכמה מקומות, מ"מ במקום שרבינו שמואל הנגיד עזב דרכי הגאון ז"ל, עזב אותם גם הראב"ד" עכ"ד. וסברא גדולה היא דכיון דר"ש הנגיד התכתב הרבה עם רבינו האיי גאון ז"ל, בהכרח כשאנו רואים שעוזב דרך ר"ש גאון, הרי הוא כאלו קורא בגרון שכך קבל מר"ה בנו ז"ל מאין המלט. וידענו כמה גדול כבודו של ר"ה בנו ז"ל ועליו יאמר ר"ש אביו ז"ל, בני אם חכם לבך ישמח לבי גם אני. "גם אני" ירצה שאפי' שבסיבת חכמתך ורוב עובייך והיקפך אני חוזר כמין ג"ם, כלומר טפל, עכ"ז אגיל ואשמח ביוצאי חלצי, ואחר שכן הרי ר"ש הנגיד קורא בגרון הכתיבה מימי עולם, ולמה נסמוך על רש"י יותר ממנו? אין זה דרך מבקר יורד חדרי בטן הביקור בשום אופן שבעולם. ומי זוטר מה שר"ש הנגיד כרוזא קרי, שלא זאת שר"הק כתב המשנה, אלא שגם החכמים הקדמונים כל אחד היה מעתיק לנפשו מה שלמד, בין דבר שהוא הלכה ובין דבר שאינו הלכה, ור"הק רוחו הוא קבצן ועשאן חיבור שלם, הרי דברים מבוררים שכתבנו יוצאים מפורשים מפי תלמיד הגאונים ממש, כמו שהוכחנו ממש שהיתה הכתיבה, אבל היתה לזכרון ולא ללמוד מתוכה וזהו אומרו "מעתיק לנפשו" שהוא ממש כתיב ולא מנח לפני כ"ע, ולבי אומר לי שאין ספק שעל תשובת ר"ש הגאון' ז"ל כבר נסתפקו בה לימים קדמונים איזה ספיקות, ושלחו לרבי' האי בנו הגדול לבארם כמו שמצינו אותה שלפנינו בקובץ זה לעיל סי' ע"א (*) וכן אין ספק, כי רבי' שמואל אסתפק בתשו' זאת במ"ש "לא אכתיבו" ואח"כ יאמר "מנסחי דכתיבי" מה ר"ל? וביאר עליה הגאון בנו שר"ל, לא אכתיבו, לא נתנו ליכתב כדי ללמוד מתוך הכתב, אלא אם כן נתנו ליכתב כל א' לעצמו לזכרון, ולעולם יהיו זהירין למגרסינהו ע"פ, כמו שכך צריך שנפרש, אי אתה כותב הלכות שהביא הגאון לראיה לדבריו, וא"כ כמו א"א כותב הלכות, ר"ל אי אתה כותב כדי ללמוד מתוכן, ואין לו פי' אחר, וכאשר הארכתי לעיל, כן "לא אכתיבו" דכתב הגאון הוא על משקל זה, ואחרי שדברי רבינו שרירא גאון מורים פי' זה ונוטין אליו, ואנו מוצאים באחד משותי מימיהם של הגאונים עצמם דכרוזא קרי בחיל הדברים כנתינתן, למה נעקש עלינו את המקראות ונתלה בטעות סופר, מה שאין לנו רשות לא מצד השכל ולא מצד הדת? ואם נסגור עינינו גם אל פנה אמתית הזאת, אין לך משפט מעוקל גדול הימנו. ה. מי לנו זקן בית התלמוד, ובקי בדברי הגאונים, ומבקר גדול, וחכם הגיוני, ובעל קריטיק, כהרמב"ם, אשר שמו לא ימחה לעולם ועד בכלל כל חכמי ישראל, והרי גם הוא קורא בגרון בהקדמתו לס' היד "דעד רבינו הקדוש, ראש ב"ד או נביא שהיה באותו הדור כותב לעצמו זכרון השמועות ששמע מרבותיו, והוא "מלמד על פה" ברבים, וכן כל א' וא' כותב לעצמו כפי כחו (ר"ל כח חכמתו, וכח הגיון לשונו, וכח קבלתו) מביאור התורה ומהלכותיו כמו ששמע, ומדברים שנתחדשו בכל דור ודור, בדינים שלא למדום מפי השמועה, אלא במדה מי"ג מדות שהתורה נדרשת, והסכימו עליהם ב"ד הגדול, וכן היה הדבר תמיד עד רבינו הקדוש והוא קיבל כל השמועות, וכל הדינים, וכל הביאורים, והפירושים וכו', בכל התורה כולה,

paragraphs.english_raw: "rooms," regarding every chapter, when he comes to speak of Rabbenu Sherira, of blessed memory, let his mouth be filled with his praise, both in the Toledot Ha'Arukh, and in the Toledot of his son Rabbenu Hai Gaon, of blessed memory, and in his introduction, full of the spirit of knowledge and fear of the Lord, which is in the Responsa of the Geonim, Berlin edition, until he wrote concerning the Iggeret of Rabbenu Sherira in the Yuchasin, which we are discussing, as follows: "And it is exceedingly wondrous in its explanation of the years of our ancient Sages, of blessed memory, and in clarifying every matter according to its truth, and in adducing the Talmudic statements pertinent to his words; and every researcher of antiquities will rejoice and be sated with delights upon reading it." (Toledot Rabbenu Nissim, B.H.A., Note 32). These are the words of a scholar of our time. May the Lord, his God, be with him and bring him up.

paragraphs.english_raw: And if we do not believe the voice of the first authority, namely Rabbenu Sherira Gaon, of blessed memory, in the two previously mentioned responsa – for it is possible that claims of forgery will be brought against the one before us, and against his Iggeret in the Yuchasin with the obscure version in Chofesh Matmonim, for its face has been covered repeatedly with omissions, as previously mentioned – then let us believe the voice of the last authority, Rabbenu Shmuel HaNagid, of blessed memory, a student of the Geonim, who through Rabbenu Nissim of Kairouan acquired this good name by means of his questions to Rabbenu Hai Gaon, of blessed memory, and by receiving his responsa from him. And he is a great tree upon whom to rely in this matter, more than Rabbi Shlomo Yitzchaki and his associates by a thousandfold. And go forth and see what the Gaon of our generation, previously mentioned, wrote in Toledot Rabbenu Hai Gaon, of blessed memory, Note 2, as follows: "Even though the Iggeret of Rabbenu Sherira in the Yuchasin was always a source for Sefer HaQabbalah of the Ra'avad, as I have demonstrated in several places, nevertheless, wherever Rabbenu Shmuel HaNagid abandoned the ways of the Gaon, of blessed memory, the Ra'avad also abandoned them." Thus far his words. And it is a significant inference, that since Rabbenu Shmuel HaNagid corresponded extensively with Rabbenu Hai Gaon, of blessed memory, it is necessarily the case that when we are concerned that he abandons the way of Rabbenu Sherira Gaon, it is as if he loudly proclaims that he received it thus from Rabbenu Hai, his son, of blessed memory, without fail.

paragraphs.english_raw: And we know how great was the honor of Rabbenu Hai, his son, of blessed memory, concerning whom his father Rabbenu Sherira, of blessed memory, said, "My son, if thy heart be wise, my heart shall rejoice, even mine." "Even mine" means that even if, because of your wisdom and your great breadth and scope, I become like a "gimel," meaning secondary, nevertheless, I shall rejoice and be glad in the offspring of my loins. And since this is so, Rabbenu Shmuel HaNagid loudly proclaims the tradition of writing from ancient times; so why should we rely on Rabbi Shlomo Yitzchaki more than upon him? This is by no means the method of a critic delving into the inner chambers of inquiry. And who is so insignificant as to proclaim, as Rabbenu Shmuel HaNagid does, that not only did Rabbenu HaQadosh write the Mishnah, but also that each of the ancient Sages transcribed for himself what he had learned, whether it was a matter of Halakhah or not a matter of Halakhah, and Rabbenu HaQadosh gathered them with his spirit and made them into a complete compilation? Behold, the clear matters we have written emerge explicitly from the mouth of a direct student of the Geonim, just as we have indeed proven that writing existed, but it was for remembrance and not for learning from it. And this is what he means by "transcribing for himself," which is truly writing, but not placed before everyone. And my heart tells me that there is no doubt that concerning the responsum of Rabbenu Sherira Gaon, of blessed memory, some doubts arose in ancient times, and they sent to Rabbenu Hai, his great son, to clarify them, as we find the one before us in this collection above, chapter 71. And likewise, there is no doubt that Rabbenu Shmuel questioned in this responsum what he wrote: "they were not written down," and afterwards he says: "from extant drafts." What does he mean? And his son, the Gaon, clarified concerning it, that he meant: "they were not written down" – they were not given to be written so as to learn from the writing, unless they were given to be written by each person for himself as a remembrance, and they should always be careful to recite them orally. Thus, we must interpret it: "You do not write Halakhot" which the Gaon brought as proof for his words. And therefore, just as "no one writes Halakhot," meaning you do not write them in order to learn from them, and it has no other interpretation. And as I have elaborated above, so too "they were not written down," which the Gaon wrote, is along these lines. And after the words of Rabbenu Sherira Gaon indicate this interpretation and incline towards it, and we find in one of the sources of the Geonim themselves that it loudly proclaims the force of the matters as they were given, why should we stubbornly twist the verses and attribute it to a scribe's error, which we are not permitted to do either by reason or by religion? And if we close our eyes even to this true aspect, there is no greater perverted judgment than this.
paragraphs.english_html: And we know how great was the honor of Rabbenu Hai, his son, of blessed memory, concerning whom his father Rabbenu Sherira, of blessed memory, said, "My son, if thy heart be wise, my heart shall rejoice, even mine." "Even mine" means that even if, because of your wisdom and your great breadth and scope, I become like a "gimel," meaning secondary, nevertheless, I shall rejoice and be glad in the offspring of my loins. And since this is so, Rabbenu Shmuel HaNagid loudly proclaims the tradition of writing from ancient times; so why should we rely on Rabbi Shlomo Yitzchaki more than upon him? This is by no means the method of a critic delving into the inner chambers of inquiry. And who is so insignificant as to proclaim, as Rabbenu Shmuel HaNagid does, that not only did Rabbenu HaQadosh write the Mishnah, but also that each of the ancient Sages transcribed for himself what he had learned, whether it was a matter of Halakhah or not a matter of Halakhah, and Rabbenu HaQadosh gathered them with his spirit and made them into a complete compilation? Behold, the clear matters we have written emerge explicitly from the mouth of a direct student of the Geonim, just as we have indeed proven that writing existed, but it was for remembrance and not for learning from it. And this is what he means by "transcribing for himself," which is truly writing, but not placed before everyone. And my heart tells me that there is no doubt that concerning the responsum of Rabbenu Sherira Gaon, of blessed memory, some doubts arose in ancient times, and they sent to Rabbenu Hai, his great son, to clarify them, as we find the one before us in this collection above, chapter 71. And likewise, there is no doubt that Rabbenu Shmuel questioned in this responsum what he wrote: "they were not written down," and afterwards he says: "from extant drafts." What does he mean? And his son, the Gaon, clarified concerning it, that he meant: "they were not written down" – they were not given to be written so as to learn from the writing, unless they were given to be written by each person for himself as a remembrance, and they should always be careful to recite them orally. And therefore, just as "no one writes Halakhot," meaning you do not write them in order to learn from them, and it has no other interpretation. And as I have elaborated above, so too "they were not written down," which the Gaon wrote, is along these lines. And if we close our eyes even to this true aspect, there is no greater perverted judgment than this.

paragraphs.english_raw: Who among us is a patriarch of the house of the Talmud, and expert in the words of the Geonim, and a great critic and logical scholar, and a master of critique, like Maimonides, whose name shall never be erased among all the Sages of Israel? For he too loudly proclaims in his Introduction to Sefer HaYad: "For before Rabbenu HaQadosh, the head of the Beit Din or a prophet who was in that generation would write for himself a record of the traditions he heard from his teachers, and he would teach orally to the public. And similarly, each one for himself, according to his ability (meaning the power of his wisdom, and the power of his logical expression, and the power of his reception), would write from the exposition of the Torah and from its Halakhot as he heard, and from matters that were innovated in each and every generation, regarding laws which they did not learn by oral tradition, but rather by one of the thirteen hermeneutical principles by which the Torah is expounded, and upon which the Great Beit Din agreed. And so was the matter always until Rabbenu HaQadosh, and he received all the traditions, and all the laws, and all the expositions, and the commentaries, etc., in the entire Torah, and compiled."
